hero.title: Aleph
hero.sub_html: Your agent intelligence — not a black box.
hero.desc: One personal agent that lives natively on your desktop and reaches you on every channel you already use — Telegram, Slack, your browser. It remembers you, runs on your terms, and quietly orchestrates a team of specialists across research, writing, code, scheduling, and the small logistics of a life.

manifesto.statement_html: We treat your assistant as a partner you can read, not a box you have to trust.
manifesto.body: Most AI hides its reasoning behind a cloud URL and hopes you don't ask. Aleph does the opposite. The brain runs on your machine; every channel — desktop, phone, browser — is just a door to the same mind. Every plan it forms, every sub-agent it dispatches, every memory it keeps, every tool it runs in its sandbox is legible, editable, and yours. Intelligence that earns trust by showing its work.

faq.title_html: On Aleph, agents, memory & the local-first question.

items.a: By default, Aleph runs on your device with your data. Memory, files, and reasoning stay local. Risky tools run in an OS sandbox and ask before acting — and when you explicitly route a task to a cloud model, you see exactly what leaves your machine.

items.q: How is this different from a single chatbot?
items.a: A chatbot answers in one window. Aleph is one brain that lives natively on your desktop and reaches you everywhere — Telegram, Slack, your browser — with the same memory and identity. It dispatches named sub-agents for research, writing, code, and logistics, runs them in parallel, and stitches the results into one finished artifact — all in a single conversation.

Every plan, every sub-agent call, and every memory Aleph keeps about you is visible and editable. You can open the trace on any task, see the reasoning, and correct it. Nothing happens in a black box.

items.q: Can I choose which AI model powers it?
items.a: Yes. Aleph is model-agnostic. Route any task to Claude, GPT, Gemini, a local Llama, or your own fine-tune — and switch providers anytime without losing your memory or your skills.

items.q: How does memory and personalization work?
items.a: Aleph keeps a private, structured memory — linked notes it can traverse, not just a vector blob — of your preferences, projects, and people, compacting and connecting them over time. It is yours: inspectable, exportable, and deletable at the level of a single fact.
